anatomy.intro: The numbered illustration explains the Mammillaria cf. rekoi candidate; it is a botanical guide, not a measured portrait.

parts.function: A raised green mound forms part of the water-storing stem.
parts.label: Tubercle

parts.function: Spines emerge from the specialized cushion at the tubercle's tip.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Numerous fine pale spokes partly screen the green body.
parts.label: Radial spines

parts.function: A stronger amber-brown spine projects outward with a curved tip.
parts.label: Hooked central spine

flowers.text: Descriptions of M. rekoi give small deep pink to purple-pink flowers with darker midribs. An observed open flower would help compare this plant with other hooked-spine species; flowering is not yet established by the available record.

growth.note: Hook shape and later flowers are more useful identification evidence than a promised age or size.

stages.text: A small rounded body carries tightly arranged tubercles.
stages.title: Bristly globe

stages.text: The stem can elongate while retaining its dense spine covering.
stages.title: Short cylinder

stages.text: Some forms produce offsets in cultivation, although wild plants may remain solitary.
stages.title: Possible clump

habitat.text: Kew places Mammillaria rekoi in Morelos, Puebla, and Oaxaca, Mexico, and describes a plant of dry shrubland that can grow on rock. This collection cactus resembles that species, but remains a qualified candidate. Other hooked-spine Mammillaria and nursery hybrids can share much of the same small, bristly outline.

A Mammillaria rekoi cactus: small solitary rounded green stem with many conical tubercles, dense fine white radial spines and several amber/reddish central spines with clearly hooked tips. 1 points to a green tubercle, 2 to an areole at its tip, 3 to the fine white radial spines, 4 to one clearly hooked amber central spine.

lookalikes.name: Silken pincushion cactus
lookalikes.text: M. bombycina has a heavier white woolly coat and commonly makes a cluster of cylindrical heads; both can have brown hooked spines.

mature.text: The species description gives stems roughly 12–15 cm tall and 5–6 cm across. These figures describe a reference taxon; the collection's unresolved identity means they are a guide rather than a firm limit.

milestones.text: Purchased at Carlsons' Greenhouse in a 4-inch individual pot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

milestones.text: Close observations recorded a green rounded body, pale radial spines, and tan-to-red central spines with hooked tips.
milestones.title: Hooked-spine comparison

nameStory.text: The species began as Neomammillaria rekoi in 1923 and was transferred to Mammillaria in 1925.
